clue.text: Boy, patient should the need arise

parts.note: a doctor's patient is a case

explanation.surface: A worried parent's thought: the boy should see a doctor if things get worse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boy' is any boy's name; here it is Justin.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for doing something as a precaution against a possible future need.

clue.text: Lift sailor

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a ... or ... tar is a seaman

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a sailor hoisting something; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means raise up with a mechanical device; as a noun it is old slang for a seaman.

clue.text: Powerful fighter in Peru stumbling into wild horse

indicators.note: a stumbling walker loses their order of steps, so these letters lose theirs
something wild is untamed and disordered, so the following word is jumbled too
one jumbled group goes into the middle of the other

parts.note: the letters of horse rearranged, split around the insertion

explanation.surface: A tough boxer stumbling around Peru and wrestling a wild horse.
explanation.walkthrough: Both anagrams are needed: UPER sits inside the rearranged horse, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A comic-book champion with special strength fighting villains is fairly called a powerful fighter.

clue.text: Expression I had attributed to Douglas's isle

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had
Douglas is the capital of the Isle of Man, abbreviated IOM

explanation.surface: A saying credited to someone from the Isle of Man's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Douglas is not a person but the main town of the Isle of Man, a self-governing island in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixed phrase whose meaning is not literal is an idiom, a kind of verbal expression.

clue.text: Heavy fruit clown dropped on head

parts.note: Coco was a famous circus clown
nut is slang for the head

explanation.surface: A clown at the circus gets a heavy fruit dropped on his head.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue one part placed on another comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: The big hard-shelled palm fruit is notably weighty, as anyone hit by a falling one learns.

clue.text: Ales drunk by worker showing what stops a leak

indicators.note: drunk means intoxicated, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A workman drinking ales on the job, perhaps a plumber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk by' looks like the worker drinking; 'drunk' is the anagram signal and 'by' sets the worker beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sealing compound is applied to joints precisely to prevent water or air escaping.

clue.text: Walk with companions in reverse

indicators.note: in reverse means read from back to front

explanation.surface: Going for a stroll with friends, but walking backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To walk can be to tread or pace, as in to go somewhere on foot one footfall at a time.

clue.text: All together, they use the thumb index first of all

indicators.note: first of all asks for the opening letter of every word

explanation.surface: A description of people who all thumb through an index together.
explanation.walkthrough: The term is Italian, used in music for a passage played by the whole orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: The musical instruction tells every performer to play at once, so it means all together.

clue.text: Bonus for each is brought in fairly

indicators.note: brought in means placed inside the following word

parts.note: quite means fairly, split to take the insertion

explanation.surface: A bonus paid per head, fairly shared out.
explanation.definitionFit: A perk, the full form of the word, is an extra benefit on top of pay, such as a bonus.

clue.text: Italian island where top Brit stripped off

parts.note: a cap is a top or lid

indicators.note: stripped off means the outer layer is removed, leaving only the middle

explanation.surface: An Italian island where a British tourist sunbathed topless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like a garment taken off, but it gives the first piece; 'stripped' applies to Brit.
explanation.definitionFit: The island in the Bay of Naples is a famous Italian holiday destination.

clue.text: Burn: react differently in nature

indicators.note: differently means arranged in another way

explanation.surface: A burn is something that makes the skin react differently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burn' looks like the definition but it starts the wordplay; the definition is the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's nature is their essential disposition or set of qualities, also called their makeup.

clue.text: Sensational, a parent with pizzazz

explanation.surface: Praise for a lively, stylish parent.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal praise meaning wonderful, astonishingly good.

clue.text: Asian country in Iran almost rebuilt European country

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter goes
in places one country inside the other word
something rebuilt is put together again in a new shape

explanation.surface: Geopolitics: rebuilding one country out of others.
explanation.walkthrough: Three countries in one clue; only the last is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Balkan nation on the Black Sea, capital Bucharest, is a member state in Europe.

clue.text: I'm leaving gold-plated cube in a casino?

indicators.note: plating covers a thing on the outside, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a gaming die; the question mark flags the playful description

explanation.surface: A gambler announcing their departure with a gilded die.
explanation.walkthrough: The gold splits around the die: A outside on the left, U on the right.
explanation.definitionFit: The French farewell is used in English to say goodbye, as someone departing would.

clue.text: Nobility high-bred, by the sound of it?

indicators.note: by the sound of it asks for a phrase heard rather than read

parts.note: bred sounds like bread, and the top crust of a loaf is high

explanation.surface: Aristocrats being described as well-bred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-bred' fits nobility literally, but heard aloud it is the top of a loaf.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names the highest social class, the aristocracy and gentry.

clue.text: Offering here

definitions.meaning: second meaning: in attendance, as at a roll call

explanation.walkthrough: Two words with no link; one is a noun, the other an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a gift given to someone and also attending or being at hand.

clue.text: Hates leading pair in romantic novel in Audible range

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new form
leading pair means the first two letters

explanation.surface: Someone who hates romantic novels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Romantic novel' reads as a book genre, but 'novel' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The distance within which a sound can be heard is the hearing range of a listener.

clue.text: Muscle I nearly forgot seen after blink of an eye

parts.note: in a trice means in an instant
a postscript adds what the writer almost left out

explanation.surface: Someone forgetting a muscle name in an instant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I nearly forgot' is what a postscript says; PS comes after the instant.
explanation.definitionFit: The large three-headed muscle at the back of the upper arm is a named muscle.

clue.text: Thrill, one having departed city, relief surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests an unexpected arrangement
having departed means that letter has left the word

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I, the letter removed

explanation.surface: The thrill and relief of someone leaving a city.
explanation.definitionFit: To excite someone intensely, as if charging them with current, is to thrill them.

clue.text: Journey of self-publicist took in new pier

indicators.note: new means freshly made, so the letters are rearranged
took in means received inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: the letters rearranged, split for the insertion

explanation.surface: A showman opening a new pier as a vanity project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Took in' looks like visiting; it places GOT inside the rearranged pier.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: a vain, self-indulgent activity is pictured as the outing of a show-off.

clue.text: Building's entrance left with image that's slightly lacking

indicators.note: slightly lacking means short by a little, so the final letter goes

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
icon, an image, without its last letter

explanation.surface: A grand entrance with a slightly disappointing picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A columned porch at the front of a building forms its entrance.

clue.text: Fantasy fruit satisfied, guzzling unspecified number

indicators.note: guzzling means swallowing, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: met, as in met a demand
n is the algebraic symbol for an unspecified number

explanation.surface: Someone gorging on fruit until full.
explanation.definitionFit: A figment of the imagination is an invented thing, a fantasy.

clue.text: Got angry after 50 per cent reduction in food, and sought edibles

indicators.note: a fifty per cent reduction keeps only half the word

explanation.surface: Someone angry after their rations were halved went searching for food.
explanation.definitionFit: To forage is to search for food, as animals or gatherers do in the wild.

clue.text: Trap feline, cheetah gutted

indicators.note: gutted means the insides are removed, leaving the outer letters

explanation.surface: Trapping a big cat, perhaps for a zoo.
explanation.definitionFit: To trap is to capture or seize, which is what the answer means as a verb.

clue.text: Discernment in head of state visiting gallery

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside a place, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: the Tate gallery in London, split for the insertion

indicators.note: head of means the first letter

explanation.surface: A head of state showing discernment on a gallery visit.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a group of London art galleries.
explanation.definitionFit: Good judgement in aesthetic matters, such as art or style, is called taste.

clue.text: Curious piece, cheesy fare

explanation.surface: An odd piece of cheesy food.
explanation.walkthrough: Welsh rarebit is a British dish of melted cheese sauce on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: The dish is essentially cheese on toast, so it is literally food made of cheese.

clue.text: Working on big house

indicators.note: working means in operation, so the letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone working on a large house, a builder perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' is called out in bingo halls when a card is complete; housey-housey is an old British name for the game.
explanation.definitionFit: The game is also known as house, and the winning shout can be either word.

clue.text: List of options from e.g. Queens University

parts.note: queens are chess pieces, also called men
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A list of courses available at Queen's University.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queens University' suggests the Belfast institution, but queens are taken as chessmen.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill of fare or a computer's selection screen presents a list of choices.

clue.text: Finished work of crossword writer, painful

parts.note: a crossword compiler is a setter, whose work is setting

explanation.surface: A setter sadly reflecting on a completed puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Something distressing or hurtful to the feelings is emotionally painful.

clue.text: Racket, one breaking schnozzle!

indicators.note: breaking means bursting into, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: schnozzle is slang for nose, split for the insertion
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A tennis racket swung into someone's big nose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Racket' suggests a tennis bat; it means din.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket is a loud unpleasant din, which is sound of a disturbing sort.

clue.text: Youth coming through gate enters

indicators.note: coming through means spanning the words that follow

explanation.surface: A young person walking in through a gate.
explanation.definitionFit: A youth is a young person aged between thirteen and nineteen, an adolescent.

clue.text: Great job, beneficial

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an exclamation of praise
second meaning: healthy, doing a person good

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is read once as congratulation, once literally as healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Said aloud it congratulates someone; read literally it describes something wholesome for a person.
